key_insight: NavTrust introduces a unified benchmark that systematically corrupts inputs to embodied navigation tasks (VLN and OGN) to quantify model trustworthiness under realistic failures, exposing robustness, calibration, and safety gaps missed by nominal evaluations.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standardized evaluation for how embodied navigation agents perform and fail under real-world corruptions and perturbations across sensory and linguistic inputs.
method: Design a corruption suite that injects systematic perturbations across modalities (vision, depth, language, sensors) and varying severity levels.
Evaluate diverse VLN and OGN agents on the corrupted inputs using unified trustworthiness metrics (robustness, calibration, safety/failure modes) and produce comparative leaderboards.
Provide reproducible tools and protocols to measure degradation patterns and identify failure modes for model diagnosis and improvement.
impact: Enables researchers and engineers to benchmark and prioritize improvements for real-world deployment by revealing brittle behaviors, guiding robust model design, and standardizing trust-focused evaluation of embodied navigation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: environment → corruption module (icons for RGB/depth/lang) → agent → metric outputs (robustness, calibration, safety).
Side-by-side bar chart: model performance on nominal vs. corrupted inputs to highlight degradation.
Heatmap: corruption type/severity vs. metric drop to visualize sensitivity and failure patterns.
Icon strip: modalities and trust metrics (camera, depth sensor, text bubble, shield for safety/calibration) for quick interpretation.
paper_title: NavTrust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness for Embodied Navigation
paper_authors: Huaide Jiang, Yash Chaudhary, Yuping Wang, Zehao Wang, Raghav Sharma
